strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN with UDP/datagram-like earliest-complete inner delivery over WBD-owned TCP-shaped FakeTCP, a conservative release operating point on a physical link at or below 100 Mbit/s, shared username/password admission for multiple independent LiveID sessions, OpenWrt TPROXY capture, and Windows TUN/Wintun-class capture.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: V2.2 shared-account two-session transport is protocol-frozen for platform integration at a conservative 40 Mbit/s aggregate-inner release operating point on the 100 Mbit/s weak shared-link qualification boundary. The corrected capacity sweep is clean and authoritative. OpenWrt routing/firewall plumbing already exists; platform integration has now started with an opaque platformproxy frame contract and a session-isolated server-side UDP egress relay. The next missing executable slice is client-side OpenWrt transparent UDP capture/return through the existing WBD app-datagram boundary, followed by transparent TCP and then the Windows TUN/Wintun-class one-shot.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Prioritize first-complete inner datagram delivery and balanced independent sessions. Never gate available systematic data on cumulative TCP repair, do not add multi-tenant identity complexity, do not change legacy FakeTCP recovery or fixed 20:20 during platform integration, and reject extra throughput if it requires hundreds of milliseconds of persistent queueing. Platform routing convenience is not a reason to reopen frozen FEC, FakeTCP, DTLS, Reality-front, ticket/LiveID, association-fanout, or one-lane semantics.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Consumed the corrected mux-load-100m authority and closed the capacity cursor. GitHub Actions run 32920925944 on head a3d8b05a875b2880c69cb4d6bada967eef8c17f9 completed bench(20), bench(100), and aggregate successfully and produced unexpired RTT20, RTT100, and aggregate artifacts. Fixed 20:20 at 40 Mbit/s aggregate inner delivered 100% with p99 21.768ms at RTT20 and 60.711ms at RTT100; at 60 Mbit/s p99 rose to 286.604/210.995ms and at 80 Mbit/s to 956.262/913.954ms. Therefore the release operating point stays at 40 Mbit/s and no 50 Mbit/s midpoint is release-critical. Recorded the decision in ADR-0010 and docs/benchmarks/v2-mux-two-session-100m.md. Then started platform integration without changing frozen transport: added internal/platformproxy WBDP frames (UDP datagram plus TCP open/data/cumulative-ack/close with FlowID and byte offsets), added a server-side UDP relay keyed by (wbd-link-server-mux service peer, FlowID) so same-account independent LiveID sessions cannot cross-route even when they reuse FlowID values, added isolation/codec tests, and added cmd/wbd-platform-proxy-server. The server relay receives full UDP replies before applying the WBDP frame limit so oversized datagrams are rejected rather than silently truncated.
continuation_cursor.current_task: Complete the first executable OpenWrt platform slice: transparent UDP TPROXY capture and transparent return on the OpenWrt/client side, feeding WBDP UDPDatagram frames through the existing local UDP application interface of wbd-link-proxy. The server-side UDP egress relay already exists. Keep the WBD transport/session stack opaque to platformproxy and do not change linkdata/FEC/DTLS/FakeTCP/Reality/ticket/LiveID semantics.
continuation_cursor.why_now: The corrected 100 Mbit/s sweep reproduced the latency cliff and ADR-0010 freezes the release transport at 40 Mbit/s aggregate inner, so more capacity work would violate the latency-first stop rule. PROJECT_CONSTITUTION requires OpenWrt TPROXY plus policy routing and mandatory underlay escape, with real DNS/TCP/UDP and cleanup in the final one-shot. scripts/openwrt_tproxy.sh already installs and removes the nft/ip state but explicitly lacked the user-space transparent adapter. wbd-link-proxy already transports opaque complete application datagrams, while wbd-link-server-mux gives each LiveID its own connected service UDP peer; those boundaries allow the platform adapter to be added above the frozen WBD link.
continuation_cursor.done_when: A Linux/OpenWrt transparent UDP adapter can bind the configured TPROXY port, recover the original UDP destination, allocate stable per-flow FlowIDs, send WBDP UDPDatagram frames to the local wbd-link-proxy app socket, map reverse WBDP frames back to the intercepted client with transparent source addressing, and cleanly expire flow state. Unit tests cover original-destination/flow mapping and no cross-flow routing; a root/network-namespace integration proves at least real DNS/UDP through the installed TPROXY+policy-routing rules with underlay escape and cleanup. Then continue with the TCP open/data/ack/close adapter required for the final real TCP gate, without reopening transport semantics.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: Implement the Linux/OpenWrt client-side transparent UDP adapter above internal/platformproxy. Use the existing scripts/openwrt_tproxy.sh default capture port 12345 unless explicitly overridden. Recover original destination from the TPROXY socket, key local flow state by intercepted client endpoint plus original destination/protocol, assign a nonzero FlowID per flow, and exchange only WBDP UDPDatagram frames with the local wbd-link-proxy UDP application socket. Reverse frames must be emitted to the intercepted client with the remote/original peer as transparent source; never route them back into WBD capture. Add deterministic non-root tests for flow identity/mapping and a Linux root/netns qualification path for TPROXY original-destination plus transparent reply. Do not add a new transport dependency, do not change FEC/FakeTCP/DTLS/session semantics, and do not start TCP work until the UDP slice is clean.

udp_like_status.outer_semantics: WBD-owned TCP-shaped raw carrier with legacy shadow recovery as the product default. SACK/RACK remains explicit experimental research. Complete inner datagram delivery never waits for cumulative TCP ACK or repair. ADR-0010 freezes this transport boundary for platform integration.
udp_like_status.fec_status: Live negotiation admits FEC off or fixed systematic 20:20 tail-RS. Surviving systematic sources stream immediately and missing originals reconstruct from repair shards; no runtime config epoch or adaptive retune is qualified. The release platform path does not change this policy.
udp_like_status.two_client_clean_gate: GitHub Actions fullstack-mux-two-client run 32911866748 SUCCESS for both FEC off and fixed 20:20: two distinct tickets from one shared account, one public FakeTCP listener, two inherited-fd wolfSSL DTLS workers, two independent LINK/LiveID sessions, concurrent unique application echoes with no cross-session routing.
udp_like_status.two_session_load_gate: Authoritative GitHub Actions mux-load-100m run 32918572671 SUCCESS at a 100 Mbit/s shared link, two simultaneous 20 Mbit/s inner streams, RTT 20/100 ms, setup loss 0 and measurement random loss 20%. Fixed 20:20 delivered 100% at both RTTs versus off about 80%; p99 increased by 9.617/10.415ms and exact fixed plaintext expansion was 2.1622x/2.1597x.
udp_like_status.capacity_diagnostic: Corrected GitHub Actions mux-load-100m run 32920925944 is the clean authority for the 40/60/80 Mbit/s aggregate-inner ceiling. Fixed 20:20 at 40M delivered 1.000 at both RTTs with p99 21.768/60.711ms; at 60M p99 was 286.604/210.995ms and RTT20 delivery fell to 0.7742; at 80M p99 was 956.262/913.954ms. Both LiveIDs remained balanced. This clean result confirms the earlier diagnostic cliff and closes release capacity at 40 Mbit/s without a midpoint retune.
udp_like_status.lifecycle: Client sends DTLS-protected WBD PING after 15s idle, handles PONG/CLOSE, and on normal stop flushes FEC then best-effort CLOSE_NORMAL. Shared link server refreshes active leases on data/control/service traffic, echoes lifecycle control via the existing state machine, and reclaims idle LiveID slots after a default 90s lease.
udp_like_status.memory_policy: Performance first: retain bounded independent state per LiveID and never gate new inner datagrams on pending repair depth merely to save memory. Platformproxy state must additionally be isolated by LiveID-facing service peer plus FlowID on the server side.
udp_like_status.capacity_policy: V2.2 release qualification is frozen at 40 Mbit/s aggregate inner on the current 100 Mbit/s weak shared-link boundary. Sixty and eighty Mbit/s are not release operating points because the clean corrected sweep shows persistent hundreds-of-milliseconds to near-one-second tail queueing. Fifty Mbit/s is optional future research, not release-critical.

product_policy.link_setup: Reality-like TLS front is connection setup only. Recognized same-entry TLS authenticates the shared username/password and issues a fresh one-time ticket; FakeTCP/DTLS then performs ticket bind and immutable LINK_INIT/LINK_ACCEPT. Sustained VPN payload never uses the front TCP stream.
product_policy.fec: Association setup admits off or fixed systematic 20:20 tail-RS. No runtime FEC config epoch; adaptive/intermediate profiles remain research until separately qualified.
product_policy.accounts: One configured shared username/password may authenticate multiple simultaneous devices. Every login gets a distinct random ticket/LiveID; live routing and FEC state are keyed by LiveID/peer, never username.
product_policy.recovery: FakeTCP product default is legacy shadow recovery. sack-rack remains opt-in experimental/diagnostic and is not a release default.
product_policy.certificate_policy: Personal client may explicitly disable certificate-chain and hostname verification for both front TLS and DTLS while encryption remains enabled and logs disclose the verification mode.
product_policy.routing: OpenWrt final capture is TPROXY plus policy routing and underlay escape; Windows final capture is TUN/Wintun-class with endpoint escape. Linux TUN remains a regression harness. Platformproxy is an application/session adapter above the frozen WBD link, not a replacement transport.
product_policy.release_gate: Protocol is frozen by ADR-0010 at the 40 Mbit/s aggregate-inner operating point. Remaining release gates are one clean OpenWrt TPROXY install -> front/FakeTCP/DTLS/LINK -> real DNS/TCP/UDP -> clean restore, then one clean Windows TUN/Wintun-class install -> same application gate -> clean restore.
